title: Thread keypoints and measurement sign into the evidence plan
description:
Plumbing prerequisite. Nothing in Epic B can draw a joint or an oriented caliper until this lands.

## Gap 1 — the plan drops the keypoints
`EvidenceFramePlan` (evidenceFrames.ts:139-154) retains only `{metric, kind, side?, quality, label, base:{timestamp,opacity}, ghost, crop, demotedFromPair}`. No RobustPoseFrame, no keypoint positions, and `cropKeypoints` is consumed inside `planExemplarFrames` (:404-429) and then DROPPED.

`robustFrames` is also not threaded into the extractor at all: `ClipEvidenceInput = { sourceBlob, plan }` (extractFrames.ts:121-124), and EvidenceGallery has `input.frames` in scope (:57, :92) but passes only `{sourceBlob, plan}` (:218).

Three viable seams. PREFER THE FIRST — `planExemplarFrames` already holds both RobustPoseFrames at :401-410, so resolving there keeps everything in the pure, unit-testable half exactly as the module already does for crop rects:
  a) resolve positions (or DrawOps) into EvidenceFramePlan during planning  <-- preferred
  b) carry cropKeypoints forward and re-resolve at draw time
  c) add frames to ClipEvidenceInput and resolve in extractFrames.ts

Resolution itself is exact: `base.timestamp`/`ghost.timestamp` are the SAMPLED frame's own timestamp (evidenceFrames.ts:438-445), so `findNearestFrame` returns exactly that frame object. Note `resolvePoint` (keypoints.ts:23-30) treats 'detected' AND 'interpolated' as resolvable; only 'unrecoverable' is null — preserve that distinction, the thumbnails should show it.

## Gap 2 — the sign is missing
`travelDirection` (±1) and `outwardSign` determine the SIGN of every offset metric — overstriding.ts:177, footStrikePattern.ts:192, trunkLean.ts:171, strideLength.ts:182, stepWidth.ts:222-223. NEITHER is carried on `MetricExemplar` nor `EvidenceFramePlan`.

Consequence: a caliper or arrow claiming 'ahead of the hip' vs 'behind', or 'own side' vs 'crossed over', CANNOT be oriented from the plan today. Without this, an overstriding mark can be drawn pointing the wrong way on a right-to-left runner and nothing will catch it.

Thread whichever of these the annotation layer needs. Keep it canvas-free — jsdom has no canvas.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Both instants' keypoint positions are resolvable by the draw layer, with detected-vs-interpolated status preserved
- [ ] travelDirection and/or outwardSign are available wherever a signed mark is drawn
- [ ] The pure/impure split holds: resolution stays canvas-free and unit-tested
- [ ] Plan shape change is covered by evidenceFrames tests
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean

title: Restructure the shell: clips leave the body, picker owns the zero-clip state
description:
The structural move, and the riskiest ticket in the epic. Everything else in Epic A depends on it.

Today `MultiClipVideoSession` renders a 2-col grid: every clip as a full `ClipSlot` stacked in a sticky left column (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:179-201), results in the right column. This ticket removes clips from the page body.

After this ticket:
- Clip video elements are MOUNTED BUT NOT LAID OUT IN THE BODY — they become hidden hosts that the modal (next ticket) reveals.
- Zero clips renders a full-page picker.
- The results column becomes the page's main content rather than one half of a grid.

## HARD CONSTRAINT — the whole reason this is its own ticket
Sampling reads frames off a live, PLAYING <video> element (`useVideoAnalysis` per clip, mounted in ClipSlot.tsx:51). Clip video elements MUST remain mounted and playable while analysing. Hiding must be visual only. Do NOT conditionally render them, do not move them behind a mount gate, and do not use `display:none` without verifying frame sampling still advances — a display:none video can be throttled or refuse to play in some engines. Prefer keeping the element in flow but visually clipped/offscreen, and VERIFY LIVE.

Type checks and unit tests will NOT catch a break here. Verify in headless Chromium on real GPU per CLAUDE.md's live-browser harness: analysis must still reach 'Analysis complete' with a normal `sampling.detectedFrames` count on Demo 1 and Demo 2.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Clips no longer occupy a body column; results are the main content
- [ ] Zero clips renders a full-page picker
- [ ] Clip video elements stay mounted and analysis still completes — VERIFIED LIVE in headless Chromium on real GPU, not by unit test alone
- [ ] `[analysis-diagnostics]` sampling.detectedFrames on Demo 1 is within normal range vs. the pre-change baseline (record both numbers in the ticket)
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean

title: Verify annotated inline evidence live in headless Chromium
description:
Per CLAUDE.md, unit tests cannot prove this works — and this epic is specifically about whether an IMAGE reads correctly to a human, which no assertion covers.

Run per CLAUDE.md's live-browser harness: headless Chromium, real GPU, confirm `ANGLE Metal Renderer` not `SwiftShader Device`. Three clips: Demo 1 (side view), Demo 2 (front view), `e2e/fixtures/multiperson-track.mp4` via upload.

## Actually LOOK at the images
Pull each rendered thumbnail out of the DOM and read it (the Read tool renders images). The prior epic's verification found three real defects this way that no test caught — a bounce ghost that reads as horizontal translation on a side view, a bystander swallowed by the 320px crop floor, and a whole-frame crop on a far-apart pair. Annotation changes all three: joints drawn on the wrong body make a bad crop obvious.

## Capture
`[evidence-coverage]` is dev-only and JSON-parseable; match it exclusively with `startsWith('[evidence-coverage]')`. TAKE THE LAST LINE, NOT THE FIRST — on a MoveNet-primary run the background MediaPipe scale pass grafts `verticalOscillationCm` in after `phase: 'ready'`, which correctly triggers a re-extraction and emits a second line. Whether a harness sees one line or two is a race against the scale pass.

## Confirm the contracts still hold
- `[analysis-diagnostics]` still carries no exemplar data, canvas, or blob URL.
- `vite build` output contains zero occurrences of any dev-only console prefix.
- Extraction adds its cost AFTER 'Analysis complete', not before — analysis wall-clock must not regress.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Renderer string confirmed real GPU, recorded
- [ ] All three clips analysed; per-metric evidence coverage recorded from the LAST [evidence-coverage] line
- [ ] Every rendered thumbnail visually inspected; joints land on the runner's actual body
- [ ] Any metric whose annotation is unreadable is reported with the reason (do not silently drop it)
- [ ] [analysis-diagnostics] payload confirmed free of image/exemplar data
- [ ] vite build output confirmed free of dev-only console prefixes
- [ ] Analysis wall-clock compared against baseline; no regression

title: Retire the standalone evidence gallery and its deep-link channel
description: Delete `src/results/EvidenceGallery.tsx` (520 lines) and unwind the reporting channel it exists to feed. ## The channel to unwind EvidenceGallery reports which metrics actually produced imagery back up via `onEvidenceMetricsChange` (EvidenceGallery.tsx:441-449) -> MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:230 -> `reportedEvidenceMetrics` state (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:82-83) -> ResultsView -> MetricsPanel, purely so a card knows whether to render `EvidenceDeepLink` (MetricsPanel.tsx:110-122, `See evidence down`). With evidence inline, the card already holds its own evidence and this entire round trip is dead. Remove it rather than leaving it wired to nothing. Also goes away: `EVIDENCE_SECTION_ID_PREFIX` (EvidenceGallery.tsx:27, shared with MetricsPanel), the `lg:col-span-2` third grid child (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:226-232), and the gallery heading 'What the analysis looked at'. ## Keep — this is the part that is easy to delete by accident The extraction ENGINE is not the gallery. `src/results/evidenceFrames.ts` (pure planning) and `src/video/extractFrames.ts` (drawing) stay and are still the source of every image. So do the per-clip extraction cache keyed by clipId, the run-id guard, and the sequential one-decoder-at-a-time discipline (extractFrames.ts:443-486). Whatever component owns extraction after this ticket must preserve: at most one detached decoder open at a time, object URL owned and revoked, and release on unmount/session reset. Sequencing: land this AFTER inline evidence renders, so there is never a build with no evidence surface at all.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] EvidenceGallery.tsx is deleted along with its test
- [ ] onEvidenceMetricsChange and reportedEvidenceMetrics are gone, not left wired to nothing
- [ ] EvidenceDeepLink and EVIDENCE_SECTION_ID_PREFIX are gone
- [ ] Extraction still runs at most once per clip, holds at most one detached decoder at a time, and releases on unmount and session reset
- [ ] No dead exports remain (`npx eslint .` clean)
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean

title: Assess annotation misregistration from the 2-frame evidence seek offset (gh #69)
description:
This epic makes an existing latent bug newly VISIBLE, which is why it is scoped here rather than left on the GitHub backlog.

## The measured bug (GitHub #69, not hypothesised)
`sequentialSampling` defaults on, so most MP4s sample through WebCodecs where `robustFrames[].timestamp` is raw `sample.cts / sample.timescale` (src/video/mp4Demux.ts:174) with NO edit-list adjustment, while `HTMLVideoElement.currentTime` IS adjusted. The evidence extractor seeks a detached <video> to the planned timestamp, so every extracted frame lands late by the clip's own `elst media_time / mediaTimescale`. Ground-truthed by ffmpeg/PSNR argmax: +2 frames on all three test clips (0.0800s on Demo 1 at 25fps; 0.033367s on Demo 2 at 59.94fps; 0.033333s on the 60fps multiperson clip). Measures EXACTLY 0 under `{ sequentialSampling: { enabled: false } }` — so it is isolated to the WebCodecs domain, not to seeking.

## Why it matters now and did not before
Today's evidence images are unannotated photographs; a 2-frame offset is invisible. Once joints are drawn from the SAMPLED frame's keypoints onto an image that is 2 frames later, the skeleton floats off the body — 80ms on Demo 1 is ~12% of a step cycle, and a runner's limbs move a lot in 80ms. The annotation will look broken even though the numbers are right.

## Do not just pick a constant
`DEFAULT_EVIDENCE_SEEK_OFFSET_SECONDS` is 0 (extractFrames.ts:80) and #69 is explicit that the correct value is per-clip AND per-sampler: it must be exactly 0 for every WebM/webcam clip and every MP4 where `canUseSequentialDecode` says no. Any single constant is wrong on two of three test clips. #69 carries two real candidate fixes: plumb a per-clip offset using `src/video/containerTiming.ts`'s existing `elst` parser, or align the domains at the demuxer.

## Scope of THIS ticket
Decide, with measurement, whether annotation is acceptable at the current offset. If not, implement one of #69's two fixes. Measure misregistration in PIXELS on a real clip, not in frames — that is the number that decides it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Misregistration quantified in pixels on Demo 1 and Demo 2 with annotation drawn
- [ ] A decision is recorded: acceptable as-is, or fixed — with the measurement behind it
- [ ] If fixed: correct on WebCodecs MP4s AND exactly 0 on WebM/webcam clips and non-sequential-decode MP4s
- [ ] No single global constant is introduced as the fix
- [ ] GitHub #69 updated with the outcome (do not close it without the user's say-so)

title: Embed evidence inline in the metric card
description:
Move evidence imagery into `MetricCard` (src/results/MetricsPanel.tsx:158-197): below the description on mobile, to the RIGHT of it on desktop. ## Card anatomy today, in DOM order 1.
tier-styled (:163-169) 2.

title from METRIC_LABELS (:170-172) 3.

value (:173-175) 4.

description from METRIC_DESCRIPTIONS (:176-178) <-- evidence goes after this 5.

confidence label (:179-181) 6. optional

caveat (:182-193) 7. `chart` slot (:194) — currently carries VerticalOscillationChart and/or EvidenceDeepLink via `cardSlot()` (:130-138) ## Breakpoint mechanism — read this before reaching for `md:` The card GRID already uses container queries (`@container grid gap-4 @lg:grid-cols-2 @3xl:grid-cols-3`, MetricsPanel.tsx:288) — the only container-query usage in the app. A card is 1, 2, or 3 across depending on the panel's width, so a VIEWPORT media query will get this wrong: a card in a 3-col layout on a wide screen is NARROW. The mobile/desktop split must be a per-CARD container query, not `md:`. ## Thumbnails, not gallery figures Today's figures are `w-56` (14rem) in a wrapping flex list (EvidenceGallery.tsx:359-364). Inline thumbnails are meaningfully smaller. The extraction output is capped at `EVIDENCE_OUTPUT_MAX_SIDE_PX = 640` (extractFrames.ts:64) and every crop shares one aspect ratio by spec, so display sizing is CSS, not a re-extraction. The canvas element is adopted into the DOM directly via `host.replaceChildren(canvas)` (EvidenceGallery.tsx:296-316) — no data URL, no blob, deliberately. Preserve that mechanism. ## Preserve A card whose metric has no evidence must render exactly as it does today: no placeholder, no empty frame, no layout shift. That guarantee is in the current spec and survives the epic.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Evidence renders inside the card, after the description
- [ ] Below the description when the card is narrow, beside it when the card is wide — driven by the CARD's container width, not the viewport
- [ ] Correct at 1-col, 2-col and 3-col card grid densities
- [ ] A card with no evidence is unchanged: no placeholder, no empty frame, no layout shift
- [ ] Images remain canvas elements adopted into the DOM; no data URL, blob, or download path is introduced
- [ ] Alt text / caption still identifies the metric, the side where per-side, and that a ghosted pair is one runner at two instants
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean

title: Author the openspec change for inline annotated evidence
description:
Spec-first ticket. No implementation. This one is unusually load-bearing because the epic REVERSES a standing prohibition — a downstream implementer who reads only the current spec will believe the work is forbidden.

  openspec new change "inline-annotated-evidence"
  openspec validate inline-annotated-evidence --strict

Capability: results-view.

## Deltas required

REMOVE (with Reason/Migration), then ADD under a fresh name — the behavior fully reverses, and per CLAUDE.md a MODIFIED block that no longer resembles the original is worse than a clean REMOVE+ADD:
- 'An evidence gallery renders below the results, grouped by metric' (L735). The gallery is gone; evidence lives in the card.
- 'Metric cards deep-link to their evidence, and are otherwise unchanged' (L770). No deep link. Note the second half of that requirement — a card with no evidence renders exactly as today, no placeholder, no empty frame, no layout shift — is still WANTED and must survive into the replacement requirement.

The single most important clause to get right, at L746 inside the gallery requirement:
  'The system SHALL NOT draw a skeleton, angle arc, reference line, or any other annotation over an
   extracted image, and SHALL NOT overlay any reference or ideal posture'
That sentence contains TWO prohibitions. Reverse the FIRST (annotating detected/measured geometry is now required). KEEP THE SECOND, explicitly and in the new requirement's own words: no reference posture, no ideal, no target overlay. Thumbnails show what was measured on this runner, never something to match. If the new spec silently drops the second half, the epic has quietly changed what the product claims.

KEEP AND EXTEND, do not rewrite: 'Evidence frames are planned purely, then extracted from a detached video element' (L648). Its purity rule ('the decision half SHALL be pure... no DOM, no canvas, no video element') now extends to annotation geometry.

Also spec: thumbnail sizing/placement in the card (below description on mobile, right on desktop), and that annotation is drawn only for metrics whose quantity is actually drawable on a still — see the per-metric determination in strides-ac9.2.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] openspec change 'inline-annotated-evidence' exists with proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md and spec deltas
- [ ] `openspec validate inline-annotated-evidence --strict` passes
- [ ] The reference/ideal-posture prohibition survives explicitly into the new requirement text
- [ ] The 'card without evidence is unchanged, no placeholder, no layout shift' guarantee survives
- [ ] The purity rule is extended to annotation geometry
- [ ] REMOVE blocks reuse exact existing requirement title text
- [ ] No src/ files changed by this ticket

title: Verify the navbar clip shell live in headless Chromium
description:
CLAUDE.md's standing rule: 'Type checking and unit tests verify code correctness, not that a change actually works end to end in a browser... verify UI/pipeline changes live before calling them done.'

Run per CLAUDE.md's 'Live-browser verification harness' section: headless Chromium, real GPU (`--headless=new --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist`), NOT SwiftShader. Confirm the renderer string is `ANGLE Metal Renderer`, not `SwiftShader Device`, before trusting any number.

Cover:
- Demo 1 (side view) and Demo 2 (front view) both reach 'Analysis complete'.
- `sampling.detectedFrames` from `[analysis-diagnostics]` is in the normal range for each clip — this is THE check that the hidden-but-mounted video elements from strides-kyu.3 did not break sampling. Compare against a pre-epic baseline captured on the same machine.
- Two clips at once: both thumbnails show their own progress, and they progress independently rather than in lockstep (only one clip holds the detector at a time).
- The modal opens on a real clip and the skeleton overlay actually draws.

Match the `[analysis-diagnostics]` prefix EXCLUSIVELY (`startsWith('[analysis-diagnostics]') && !startsWith('[analysis-diagnostics:')`) or the scale-pass line collides with it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Renderer string confirmed as real GPU, recorded in the ticket
- [ ] Demo 1 and Demo 2 both reach 'Analysis complete'
- [ ] sampling.detectedFrames recorded before and after, both in normal range
- [ ] Two-clip run shows independent per-thumbnail progress
- [ ] Modal opens and the skeleton overlay draws on a real clip
- [ ] Numbers pasted into the ticket, not just 'looked fine'

title: Update component and e2e tests for the navbar clip shell
description:
The redesign moves selectors that existing tests drive.

## E2E — will break
`e2e/multiPersonAcquisition.spec.ts` drives: `getByRole('button', { name: 'Upload' })` (:40), `locator('input[type=file]')` (:41), `getByText(/analyzing|processing results/i)` (:43), `getByText(/analysis complete/i)` (:44). ## Component tests touching moved surfaces
src/App.test.tsx, src/results/MultiClipVideoSession.test.tsx, src/results/ClipSlot.test.tsx, src/results/ResultsView.test.tsx, src/video/VideoInputPanel.test.tsx.

Add coverage for what is new: the clip strip renders one thumbnail per clip; per-clip progress reflects that clip's own state and not the aggregate; the modal opens, traps focus, closes on Esc and restores focus.

CLAUDE.md is explicit that type checks and unit tests do not prove a pipeline/UI change works — this ticket owns the automated layer; live verification is strides-kyu.9.

title: Add the navbar quick action to record or upload another clip
description:
A quick action in the navbar to add another clip, replacing the in-body 'Add another clip' block (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:194-201) once >=1 clip exists. ## What exists today - Session-level add: `addClip` (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:92-96) mints an id and records a `pendingLoad`; the slot consumes it once on mount (ClipSlot.tsx:70-83). - The in-body affordance is a bordered block with a

label plus a bare ` addClip(f)} />`. `FileUpload` is `multiple` (FileUpload.tsx:44) and fires `onSelected` once per file, so one picker interaction can create N clips — preserve that. - The picker's record path is `WebcamCapture`; the tabs live in `VideoInputPanel` (Record | Upload — two tabs, not three; demo buttons are a separate row at VideoInputPanel.tsx:83-93). The quick action must offer BOTH record and upload, not upload only — the current in-body affordance is upload-only, which is a gap this ticket closes. Zero-clip state keeps the full-page picker (strides-kyu.3); this action is what the picker collapses INTO.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Navbar quick action offers both record and upload
- [ ] Selecting multiple files in one interaction still creates one clip per file
- [ ] The in-body 'Add another clip' block is removed
- [ ] The action is keyboard reachable and labeled
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean

title: Add the clip preview modal with the skeleton overlay
description:
Clicking a navbar clip thumbnail opens a modal showing that clip's video preview with the pose skeleton/wireframe overlay.

## Reuse
`SkeletonOverlay` (src/results/SkeletonOverlay.tsx:47) already does exactly this over a live <video>: canvas absolutely positioned over the element, native canvas pixels = video-native pixels, rAF sync while playing plus one-shot redraw on seeked/timeupdate. Props are `{ videoRef, frames: RobustPoseFrame[], metadata }`. Its current call site is ClipSlot.tsx:99-103, gated on `phase === 'ready' && robustFrames && metadata`.

Note the component is coupled to a LIVE video element and its media events — it cannot render against a static image. That is fine here; the modal shows the real element.

## Interaction with the previous ticket
The clip's video element is already mounted (hidden) after strides-kyu.3. The modal REVEALS the existing element — it must not mount a second video element for the same clip, and must not remount the existing one.

## Loop behavior
results-view spec L174 requires the video to loop once analysis is ready. With clips hidden, a per-clip hidden looping video burns GPU continuously. strides-kyu.1 decides and specs this; implement whatever that change specifies.

Accessibility: focus trap, Esc to close, `aria-modal`, focus returns to the originating thumbnail on close, and the overlay canvas stays `aria-hidden`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Clicking a navbar thumbnail opens a modal with that clip's video and skeleton overlay
- [ ] The modal reveals the already-mounted element; no second video element is created for the clip and the existing one is not remounted
- [ ] Overlay stays in sync during playback and on seek while paused (the existing overlay-sync behavior is preserved)
- [ ] Esc closes, focus is trapped while open, focus returns to the originating thumbnail on close, aria-modal is set
- [ ] Loop behavior matches whatever strides-kyu.1's openspec change specifies
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean

title: Render the navbar clip strip with per-clip progress on each thumbnail
description:
Put the clip strip in the navbar next to the 'Strides' wordmark (src/App.tsx:17-28 — today the header holds only an h1 and a tagline).

One thumbnail per clip, each showing that clip's OWN processing progress as an overlay on the thumbnail.

## The progress data already exists — do not build a new state machine
Per-clip `VideoAnalysisState` carries its own `phase` and `progress` (src/results/types.ts:39-59), one instance per clip via ClipSlot.tsx:51, already collected by the parent as `clipStates: Record<string, ClipSession>` (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:76). Read that.

Today progress is rendered GLOBALLY from the aggregate in ResultsView.tsx:97-123 ('Analyzing… 42%' / 'Processing results…' / 'Analysis complete.'). Per-clip progress has never been rendered anywhere except the 'Queued — waiting for another clip to finish analyzing…' line at ClipSlot.tsx:106-108.

Phases to represent: 'idle' | 'sampling' | 'processing' | 'ready' | 'error' (src/results/types.ts:6). A queued clip (one not currently holding the shared detector) needs a distinct visual from an actively-sampling one — only one clip holds the detector at a time (multiClipAnalysis.ts:163-172).

Accessibility: progress must be announced, not conveyed by the overlay graphic alone. Keep a `role="status"` text equivalent.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Clip strip renders in the navbar beside the wordmark, one thumbnail per clip
- [ ] Each thumbnail shows that clip's own progress, sourced from its per-clip VideoAnalysisState
- [ ] Sampling / processing / ready / error / queued are visually distinguishable, and by more than color alone
- [ ] Progress is available to assistive tech as text, not graphic-only
- [ ] Strip is usable at narrow widths (overflow/scroll rather than wrapping the navbar)
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean

title: Derive and expose a poster thumbnail per clip
description:
Net-new capability. Clips have NO thumbnail/poster/label concept today — `ClipSession` is `{ clipId, videoSource, analysis }` (src/results/multiClipAnalysis.ts:18-22) and clips are referenced positionally only ('From clip 1 of 2').

Derive a small poster image per clip so the navbar strip has something to render.

Where: the clip's own video element is already mounted and its metadata (width/height) is known once `videoSource.status === 'ready'` (src/video/types.ts:24-44). Draw one frame to a small offscreen canvas.

Keep the pure/impure split the repo already uses: any sizing/aspect math is canvas-free and unit-testable; only the draw touches a context. jsdom has no canvas (src/test/canvasTestUtils.ts).

Do NOT serialize the poster to a data URL or blob — hold the canvas/ImageBitmap in memory for the session, same rule the evidence path follows (results-view spec L688).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each clip exposes a poster image once its video source is ready
- [ ] Poster derivation does not disturb the clip's own playback position or analysis (sampling reads off the live element)
- [ ] Sizing/aspect math is unit-tested with no canvas dependency
- [ ] Poster is not serialized to a data URL, blob, or storage
- [ ] Poster is released on clip removal and session reset
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean

title: Evidence moves inline into annotated metric-card thumbnails
description:
Dissolve the standalone evidence gallery into the metric cards, and annotate each image with the
geometry the metric was actually derived from.

## Target end state
- Each metric card embeds its own image evidence inline: below the description on mobile, to the RIGHT
  of it on desktop.
- Evidence images become small thumbnails (today they are 14rem-wide gallery figures).
- Each thumbnail is ANNOTATED: the detected joints, plus the specific measurement geometry that metric
  computes (e.g. trunkLean = torso vector + vertical reference + angle arc; kneeFlexion = hip-knee-ankle
  chain + angle arc; stepWidth = lateral ankle separation caliper).
- `EvidenceGallery.tsx` is REPLACED by this, not kept alongside. Decided — do not re-litigate.

## Spec reversal — this is deliberate, not an oversight
`openspec/specs/results-view/spec.md` L746 currently states:
  "The system SHALL NOT draw a skeleton, angle arc, reference line, or any other annotation over an
   extracted image"
This epic reverses exactly that clause. IMPORTANT: reverse ONLY the ban on annotating detected/measured
geometry. The adjacent ban on overlaying a REFERENCE OR IDEAL POSTURE STAYS — thumbnails show what was
measured, never a target to match.

Also reversing: L735 "An evidence gallery renders below the results, grouped by metric" (full reversal —
prefer REMOVE with Reason/Migration + ADD under a fresh name, per CLAUDE.md), and L770 "Metric cards
deep-link to their evidence, and are otherwise unchanged" (no deep link; evidence is in the card).

KEEP AND EXTEND, do not rewrite: L648 "Evidence frames are planned purely, then extracted from a
detached video element". It already computes crops in video-native pixel space from the exemplar's
named keypoints — exactly the data the joint overlay needs.

## HARD CONSTRAINTS
1. jsdom in the unit suite has NO canvas (`getContext()` unimplemented; the repo deliberately refuses the
   `canvas` npm package — see src/test/canvasTestUtils.ts). Annotation geometry MUST live in a pure,
   canvas-free, unit-testable layer; only the final draw touches a rendering context. This mirrors the
   existing rule at results-view L655.
2. Extracted images stay in-memory for the session only — no data URL, no blob, no download, no
   persistence (results-view L688). Today the canvas ELEMENT is adopted into the DOM via
   `replaceChildren` (EvidenceGallery.tsx:296-316); `toDataURL`/`toBlob` are deliberately absent.
3. Evidence must never enter the `[analysis-diagnostics]` console payload (results-view L795) — its
   shape is a live-verification harness contract.

## Reuse, don't reinvent
`src/results/skeletonGeometry.ts` already emits pure point/edge DRAW OPS off `SKELETON_EDGES` with a
detected-vs-interpolated opacity distinction (`toDrawOps`). Reuse that model for the joint layer. Do NOT
write a second skeleton renderer. Note `SkeletonOverlay` the COMPONENT is coupled to a live `<video>`
and its media events — it cannot render against a static image; the reusable half is `toDrawOps`.

## Layout note
`MetricsPanel`'s card grid already uses CONTAINER queries (`@container`, `@lg:grid-cols-2`,
`@3xl:grid-cols-3` — MetricsPanel.tsx:288), the only container-query usage in the app. The
"below on mobile / right on desktop" split inside a card is a per-CARD container query, not a viewport
media query.

## Related (context only, do not close)
- GitHub #71 "Two evidence ghosts are unreadable" — whole-frame crops on far-apart pairs, and bystanders
  inside the 320px crop floor. Directly relevant: thumbnails are SMALLER, so crop quality matters more,
  and joint annotation makes a wrong-subject crop visible. Assess whether this epic subsumes part of it.
- GitHub #70 "extreme-role 1.5-MAD gate unreachable for overstriding" — overstriding emits no evidence on
  any clip measured, so that card gets no thumbnail regardless.
- GitHub #69 "Evidence seek lands 2 frames late on every MP4" — REAL INTERACTION: annotation drawn from
  sampled-frame keypoints onto a 2-frames-late image will be visibly misregistered. Joints will appear
  to float off the body. This epic makes an existing latent bug newly visible.

title: Clips live in the top navbar
description:
Move clip management out of the page body and into the top navbar, next to the "Strides" wordmark.

## Target end state
- A clip strip in the navbar: one thumbnail per clip.
- A quick action in the navbar to record/upload another clip. It replaces the in-body "Add another clip" block once >=1 clip exists.
- Clicking a clip thumbnail opens a modal with that clip's video preview + the pose skeleton/wireframe overlay.
- Per-clip processing progress renders as an overlay ON that clip's navbar thumbnail — not as a separate global banner.
- Zero clips keeps a full-page picker; it collapses into the navbar quick-action once a clip exists.

## Why this is a restructure, not a re-style
Today `MultiClipVideoSession` renders every clip as a full-height `ClipSlot` stacked in a left column,
with a single GLOBAL aggregate progress line in `ResultsView`. There is no clip list UI, no tab bar, no
selector, and no per-clip label or thumbnail anywhere in the model — clips are positional only
(`ClipSession = { clipId, videoSource, analysis }`, src/results/multiClipAnalysis.ts:18-22).

## HARD CONSTRAINT — read before touching anything
Sampling reads frames off a live, PLAYING `<video>` element. Clip video elements MUST stay mounted while
analysing. Do NOT render them only when the modal is open — the modal reveals an already-mounted element.
Getting this wrong silently breaks analysis with no type or test error.

## Spec work
One openspec change covering this epic. Affected capabilities: `results-view`, `video-input`,
`multi-clip-analysis`. Notably `results-view` L174 "Video loops with overlay once analysis is ready"
needs revisiting — a hidden looping video per clip burns GPU, so the loop should likely be scoped to
modal-open.

## Known landmines
- The sticky header height is hardcoded as `86px` in three places (MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:182,203)
  and `150px` in VideoInputPanel.tsx:132. A taller navbar breaks all four.
- `e2e/multiPersonAcquisition.spec.ts` drives real selectors this redesign moves:
  `getByRole('button', {name:'Upload'})`, `locator('input[type=file]')`, `getByText(/analysis complete/i)`.

## Related (context only, do not close)
GitHub #23 "Make results layout sticky" is SUPERSEDED by this epic — the two-column video/metrics
layout goes away entirely. Recommend closing it as superseded; that call is the user's.

title: Derive the header offset instead of hardcoding 86px and 150px
description:
The sticky header's height is hardcoded in four places and derived from nothing:
- MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:182 — `lg:top-[86px]`
- MultiClipVideoSession.tsx:203 — `lg:max-h-[calc(100vh-86px)]`
- VideoInputPanel.tsx:132 — `max-h-[calc(100vh-150px)]`
(plus whatever the restructure in strides-kyu.3 leaves behind)

Adding a clip strip to the navbar changes its height, so every one of these silently goes wrong. Either derive the offset from the actual rendered header, or single-source it as one token both the header and its dependents read.

Small ticket, but it is a real correctness bug the moment the navbar grows — worth isolating so it does not get lost inside a larger change.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] No hardcoded header-height pixel value remains in layout math
- [ ] The offset tracks the navbar's real height, including when the clip strip is present vs absent
- [ ] Verified at narrow and wide viewports
- [ ] `npm test` and `tsc -b` clean
